description:
## RDPS-to-HRDPS U-Net downscaling

`ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet-workflow` runs the Resoterre climate downscaling pipeline:
it selects Regional Deterministic Prediction System (RDPS) forecast files for a requested time range,
downloads those files, and applies a trained U-Net to produce HRDPS-scale downscaled fields.
This workflow performs inference, not model training.

### Interacting blocks and artefacts

All **Examples** of this block describe one single use case, the RDPS-to-HRDPS U-Net inference
job `d6f937f0-bdae-4dd5-9fa3-9e0686ed6715`, each from a different angle. The graph below shows how
the example artefacts (yellow) relate to each other, to the blocks of this register (blue),
to the imported blocks that define them (grey, `ogc.` prefix omitted) and to the published
or runtime resources (green). Arrows from an artefact to a block indicate the block it conforms to.

![Interactions between the blocks, example artefacts and runtime resources of the U-Net workflow](https://crim-ca.github.io/bblocks-process-profiles/_sources/downscaling-unet/workflow/diagrams/bblocks-interactions.svg)

The graph is defined in
[`diagrams/bblocks-interactions.mmd`](https://github.com/crim-ca/bblocks-process-profiles/blob/master/_sources/downscaling-unet/workflow/diagrams/bblocks-interactions.mmd)
as a Mermaid flowchart. Run `python scripts/generate_unet_diagrams.py` to refresh the SVG files.

### Model and activity classification

The central operation is **machine-learning inference for climate-variable downscaling**.
The trained Resoterre U-Net is characterized by the **Resoterre RDPS to HRDPS U-Net MLM item**
in the [STAC Machine Learning Model block](bblocks://ogc.contrib.stac.extensions.mlm).
That example describes the model's inputs and outputs, tensor structures, training metadata,
runtime requirements and associated STAC extensions. The
[published model Item](https://hirondelle.crim.ca/stac/collections/stac-mlm-examples/items/ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet)
connects the executable process to that model characterization.
The [STAC Browser view](https://hirondelle.crim.ca/stac-browser/collections/stac-mlm-examples/items/ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet)
provides an interactive presentation of the same Item. Machine-readable model references use the STAC API URL.

The workflow is both an **ML activity** and a **geoprocessing activity**:
it applies a trained model to new inputs, making it an inference activity, and transforms
georeferenced RDPS climate fields into finer-resolution HRDPS-scale fields, making it spatial
data processing. These are complementary classifications of the same operation, not alternative
labels. The workflow references the
[ML activity types profile](bblocks://ogc.model.registered-item.ml-activity-types) and
[geoprocessing activity types profile](bblocks://ogc.model.registered-item.geoprocessing-activity-types);
its process-type example records the climate-downscaling and climate-downscaling-inference
activity types. File selection and download prepare the model inputs rather than train the model.

The **Activity types, model bindings and inference enrichment** example supplies the actual
candidate type definitions, spatial/ML entity contracts, procedure links and submitted registration
metadata. Its selectable Turtle snippets reuse the imported classes and select the model's two input
specifications and one output specification in the published Item without duplicating their tensors.
The captured U-Net step is enriched separately from the original CWLProv records and references
the versioned Resoterre runtime environment, including its framework and model dependencies.

No governed register action has been established for this execution. Because the upstream ML
execution class also requires such an action, the enrichment uses a PROV execution with a `dct:type`
classification, not a claim of full upstream ML execution-profile conformance. Logical model-ready
inputs and predictions are explicitly marked as reconstructed, not individually captured tensors.

The **Published STAC MLM model Item (external source)** example includes the actual Item fetched
at build time. It shows the named inputs/outputs, tensor structures, geometry, bounding box and
temporal properties beside the RDF bindings. Structure bindings select the existing tensor contracts.
The extent bindings additionally materialize a GeoSPARQL WKT geometry in longitude/latitude CRS84
and OWL-Time timestamp literals from the selected source values. These are source-derived RDF views
provided for readability, but original material remains referenced through explicit `oa:hasSource` links.
The semantic validation script checks their equality with the live Item and fails on drift.
The model-specific inference type declares both domains through `dct:spatial` and `dct:temporal`.
The generic climate-downscaling type does not acquire this particular model's limits since they are
distinctively applicable to various climate model implementations and training constraints.
Each spatial input/output class links to its corresponding model specification, and reconstructed
entities link to both model domains through `pp:modelSpatialDomain` and `pp:modelTemporalDomain`.
These domains are not validity interval for the input or output data entities, only the recommended
and applicable domains that the model itself was designed for. The inferred forecast valid-time
interval is recorded separately from execution timestamps and the model's declared temporal domain.

The enrichment's PROV association references the exact packed CWL plan in the captured provenance,
linked to its pinned source CWL. Explicit reified statements display every ML predicate mapping,
including framework, performed tasks, inputs/outputs and structure. They describe, but do not assert,
the upstream domain-entailing predicates while the register-action modelling conflict is unresolved.
`rim:validityStatus` is the normal imported RIM predicate, distinct from publication status.
Local type definitions use `dcat:version "0.1"`; RIM has no `rim:version` property. This definition
version is distinct from the deployed model/software version `0.1.3-dev.10`.

The standard postprocessor checks the rendered examples and the missing-input/specification cases.
For the complete merged-graph check, run `python scripts/validate_unet_semantics.py` from the register root.
This also checks live model selectors, exact source-derived geometry and temporal endpoints,
and rejects missing spatial/output type declarations, extent literals and applicability links.
It requires pySHACL 0.30 or later: the postprocessor's older 0.21 validator does not enforce those
upstream nested activity-type constraints reliably.

### Processing steps

The sequence follows the descriptions and input/output contracts of the three component processes:

1. [Generate file list](bblocks://ospd.process-profiles.downscaling-unet.generate-file-list)
   (`ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-generate-file-list`) selects the RDPS forecast files needed to cover
   `start_datetime` through `end_datetime`. It prepends `data_root` to each file reference and writes
   the `forecast_files` text file. `requires_previous_forecast_step` includes the preceding forecast
   step needed for cumulative variables such as precipitation. `include_year_month_subdirectory`
   controls whether the paths include year/month directories or use a flat layout.
2. [Download files](bblocks://ospd.process-profiles.downscaling-unet.download-files)
   (`ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-download-files`) reads the file list and downloads its entries into
   the working directory exposed as `input_data`. Its process description supports HTTP(S) URLs
   and local paths accessible from the execution container.
3. [U-Net inference](bblocks://ospd.process-profiles.downscaling-unet.unet)
   (`ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet`) reads the input NetCDF directory and runs RDPS-to-HRDPS
   downscaling over the requested time range. The inference image includes the trained model,
   regridding matrices, geophysical fields, and default configuration. An optional `config` YAML
   file overrides that configuration; the workflow also passes the requested start/end datetimes.

### Inputs and results

The required inputs are `start_datetime` and `end_datetime`. Optional inputs control forecast-step
selection, source path layout, the data root, and the inference configuration.
The workflow returns `forecast_files`, the selected source-file list, and `inference_output`,
a Zarr directory containing the inference results. The downloaded NetCDF directory is an intermediate
passed between the download and inference steps, not a separate workflow output.

### Execution examples and provenance

The **Examples** tab includes the CWL workflow application package, its OGC API process description,
the Application Package deployment reference and the process-type register entry linking the
workflow to its model and activity classifications. The **execution request** example provides
the JSON `inputs` body for the illustrated 2024-05-02 time range, the process execution endpoint,
and headers for asynchronous submission. The optional configuration is omitted to use the
inference image's default configuration.

The **CWLProv execution provenance** example records job
`d6f937f0-bdae-4dd5-9fa3-9e0686ed6715`, captured on 2026-09-28. It describes the workflow
and individual step runs, their plans, input/output entities, associated agents and PROV
relationships. Turtle, expanded JSON-LD, N-Triples, PROV-JSON, PROV-N and PROV-XML representations
are provided with links to their definitions in
[the PROV representation register](https://ogcincubator.github.io/bblocks-prov-jsonld-alt/).
The captured packed CWL and job-input document are also linked from that example, so the execution
metadata can be inspected alongside the workflow and submitted input values. The supplied metadata
are not a complete BagIt archive of the execution's data payloads.

The diagram below is a synthetic view of this CWLProv capture, generated by `scripts/prov_synth.py`.
It shows the job and wrapping workflow runs, the agents, the three step runs matched to their
process profiles, the submitted inputs and the two results. Data links between steps are declared
in the CWL wiring and not observed in the captured records, and are drawn as such.

![Synthetic view of the CWLProv execution provenance of job d6f937f0](https://crim-ca.github.io/bblocks-process-profiles/_sources/downscaling-unet/workflow/diagrams/execution-provenance.svg)

The provenance content aligns with the process, job, input/output and agent relationships described
in [draft OGC API - Processes - Part 5: Provenance](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/26-038.html).
Metadata alignment does not by itself establish server conformance to that draft.

examples.content:
**All the examples of this block describe one single use case**, the RDPS-to-HRDPS U-Net inference job
`d6f937f0-bdae-4dd5-9fa3-9e0686ed6715`. They are not distinct examples. Each one shows a different facet of
the same workflow: its CWL Application Package, process description, deployment, process type, model and
activity semantics, execution request and captured provenance. The graph below shows how they relate to
each other and to the blocks that define them. Blue boxes are blocks of this register, yellow boxes are
the artefacts of the examples, grey boxes are imported blocks (`ogc.` prefix omitted) and green boxes are
published or runtime resources.

![Interactions between the blocks, example artefacts and runtime resources of the U-Net workflow](https://crim-ca.github.io/bblocks-process-profiles/_sources/downscaling-unet/workflow/diagrams/bblocks-interactions.svg)

CWL Workflow deployed as `ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet-workflow`. Its steps are described by the
`ospd.process-profiles.downscaling-unet.generate-file-list`, `ospd.process-profiles.downscaling-unet.download-files`
and `ospd.process-profiles.downscaling-unet.unet` building blocks.
The resoterre tag `0.1.3-dev.10` counterpart is <https://github.com/Ouranosinc/resoterre/blob/f08a79b9a1906a8752c5774b050e90f81f2d1bcb/examples/deploy/downscaling_unet_workflow.cwl>.

inputs:
  start_datetime:
    type: string
    doc: Start datetime in ISO 8601 format, for example 2024-05-01T07:00:00.
  end_datetime:
    type: string
    doc: End datetime in ISO 8601 format, for example 2024-05-01T08:00:00.
  requires_previous_forecast_step:
    type: boolean
    default: true
    doc: |
      Whether the previous forecast step is required. Must be true for cumulative variables,
      such as precipitation.
  include_year_month_subdirectory:
    type: boolean
    default: true
    doc: |
      Whether the listed paths include the year/month subdirectory, as on thredds (true),
      or are stored in a flat directory (false).
  data_root:
    type: string
    default: "https://pavics.ouranos.ca/twitcher/ows/proxy/thredds/fileServer/birdhouse/disk3/ouranos/geoconnections/RDPS/"
    doc: Root location prepended to each listed file, used to download the RDPS files.

    type: ["null", File]
    format:
    - "iana:application/yaml"
    - "edam:format_3750"
    doc: Optional inference configuration YAML overriding the one built into the Docker image.

  forecast_files:
    type: File
    format: iana:text/plain
    outputSource: ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-generate-file-list/forecast_files
  inference_output:

      include_year_month_subdirectory: include_year_month_subdirectory
      data_root: data_root
    out: [forecast_files]

  ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-download-files:  # downscaling_download_files
    doc: Download the listed RDPS files into a flat local directory.
    run: ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-download-files.cwl # when executing with weaver use  ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-download-files
    in:
      file_list: ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-generate-file-list/forecast_files
    out: [input_data]

  ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet:  # downscaling_unet
    run: ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet.cwl
    in:
      config: config
      input_data: ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-download-files/input_data
      start_datetime: start_datetime
      end_datetime: end_datetime
    out: [inference_output]

examples.title: (4/10) Process-type register entry
examples.content:
Register entry for the `ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet-workflow` process type, which ties all elements together.
The `processType` is a URI that identifies the process type in the *OGC API - Processes* register.
The `processDescription` identifies the deployed process and links its description at `href`.
The `plan` is the OGC Application Package at `/package`, whose `executionUnit` is the pinned CWL.
The `phase` and `profile` provide higher-level representation and cateogies that characterize the workflow.
The `provenanceClass` is represented as [`wfprov:WorkflowRun`](http://purl.org/wf4ever/wfprov#WorkflowRun)
in alignment with the generated provenance metadata obtained from the job execution of the workflow process.

examples.title: (5/10) Published STAC MLM model Item (external source)
examples.content:
Fetched from the published STAC API when this register is built, not maintained as a local copy.
Inspect `properties.mlm:input` for `rdps_inputs` and `hrdps_geophysical_inputs`, and
`properties.mlm:output` for `hrdps_outputs`. Each definition includes its tensor contract.
`geometry` and `bbox` describe the model's declared spatial domain; `start_datetime` and
`end_datetime` are the Item's declared temporal domain, not the captured job's execution dates.
The RDF temporal binding uses those two endpoints explicitly; it does not use `datetime`
as a substitute or treat the absence of a single timestamp as a missing temporal extent.

examples.title: (6/10) Activity types, model bindings and inference run enrichment
examples.content:
The Turtle selections below define the candidate climate-downscaling and inference activity types,
specialising the imported geoprocessing and ML activity-type classes rather than copying them.
They declare spatial and ML input/output entity types and reference the existing CWL procedure.
The status `rim:invalid` means the submitted candidates are not yet in force.
Status `rim:published` means their definitions are visible. It does not mean they have been approved.
The `rim:validityStatus` is the vocabulary's normal predicate, independent of publication status.
The `dcat:version` supplies the local definition version (`0.1`), not the model/software release (`0.1.3-dev.10`).

The model bindings select the existing `rdps_inputs`, `hrdps_geophysical_inputs` and `hrdps_outputs`
definitions in the published STAC Item using Web Annotation selectors and RFC 6901 JSON Pointers.
They do not copy tensor shapes or mint fragment identifiers on the STAC server. The Item remains
the authority for model contracts; these bindings are partial RDF views of its input/output definitions.

The enrichment reuses the captured U-Net step's UUID. It describes logical inputs and
outputs reconstructed from the model and procedure, not independently captured tensors or measured
tensor shapes. The original six CWLProv serializations are unchanged.

The upstream ML execution class also inherits `rim:RegisterAction`, but no governed register action
has been established for this run. The enrichment therefore uses `dct:type` for its activity-type
classification and PROV predicates for model/data usage, rather than asserting an upstream ML
execution `rdf:type` or using domain-entailing `mlact:model`/`mlact:input`/`mlact:output` predicates.
Full ML execution-profile conformance is not claimed. The activity-type definitions and typed
input/output entities are checked against the imported shapes; local shapes check the enrichment's
model, tasks, inputs and outputs without fabricating registration metadata or a register action.

examples.title: (7/10) Published MLM input and output bindings
examples.content:
Partial RDF views of the model input and output definitions.
The *selectors* identify the corresponding JSON objects in the published STAC Item.
Tensor structures, geometry and temporal-domain properties are selected too. Follow `dct:hasPart`
to the selected structure and its JSON Pointer. The geometry and start/end endpoints additionally
have source-derived GeoSPARQL WKT and OWL-Time timestamp literals, checked against the live Item
by `scripts/validate_unet_semantics.py`. CRS84 preserves GeoJSON longitude/latitude coordinate order.
The model-specific inference type references these domains through `dct:spatial` and `dct:temporal`.
Model-domain spatiotemporal references do not assert that the run covered the entire declared model domain.
Intead, they indicate the potential domains for which the model may be reasonably applied to generate inference
outputs, and for which the authors consider its invocation aligned with its training data and geophysical properties.
Data domains must be inspected from the source input data and generated inference outputs themselves and respectively.

examples.title: (8/10) Captured U-Net inference run enrichment
examples.content:
Semantic enrichment of the captured U-Net step, with reconstructed logical inputs and outputs.
Merges this resource with the activity definitions, model bindings and original CWLProv graph.
Its qualified association uses the exact packed CWL plan already identified by CWLProv.
Requested forecast valid times are separate from execution timestamps and the model's temporal domain.
The logical input/output entities reference both model applicability domains, not measured coverage.
This does not assign forecast times to static geophysical data or claim spatial/temporal containment.

Reified `rdf:Statement` resources show the exact `mlact:model`, `mlact:framework`,
`mlact:performsTask`, `mlact:input`, `mlact:output` and `mlact:structure` mappings.
RDF reification describes these statements without asserting them: it deliberately does not
entail the upstream register-action classification. Framework and task/data connections are
asserted separately through PROV and Dublin Core. Full upstream ML execution conformance remains
pending clarification of the upstream class's register-action requirement.

examples.title: (9/10) U-Net workflow execution request
examples.content:
Submit the JSON body below to
`POST https://hirondelle.crim.ca/weaver/processes/ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet-workflow/execution`
with `Content-Type: application/json`, `Accept: application/json`, and `Prefer: respond-async`.
The optional `config` input is omitted so the workflow uses its default inference configuration.
The response identifies the job to monitor; this example does not submit a job automatically.

examples.title: (10/10) U-Net workflow execution provenance (CWLProv)
examples.content:
CWLProv captured from job `d6f937f0-bdae-4dd5-9fa3-9e0686ed6715` on 2026-09-28.
The records describe the `ogc-ospd2026-downscaling-unet-workflow` execution and its three steps.
This is the provenance of the same job as the other examples, not a separate scenario.

![Synthetic view of the CWLProv execution provenance of job d6f937f0](https://crim-ca.github.io/bblocks-process-profiles/_sources/downscaling-unet/workflow/diagrams/execution-provenance.svg)

These CWLProv metadata align with the provenance content model described in the
[draft OGC API - Processes - Part 5: Provenance (26-038)](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/26-038.html):
the executed process, job activity, input/output entities, associated agents, and their
PROV relationships. The draft also describes job provenance retrieval and content negotiation
across PROV representations. This example illustrates metadata alignment, not a certification
of server endpoint or full draft conformance.

All six serializations are available in the tabs below. Their representation definitions are provided
by the [PROV register](https://ogcincubator.github.io/bblocks-prov-jsonld-alt/):

| Serialization | Representation definition |
| --- | --- |
| Turtle and N-Triples | [W3C PROV-O / RDF](bblocks://ogc.ogc-utils.prov.w3c-prov-rdf) |
| Expanded JSON-LD | [W3C PROV-O / RDF](bblocks://ogc.ogc-utils.prov.w3c-prov-rdf), related to [PROV-JSONLD](bblocks://ogc.ogc-utils.prov.w3c-prov-jsonld) |
| PROV-JSON | [W3C PROV-JSON](bblocks://ogc.ogc-utils.prov.w3c-prov-json) |
| PROV-N | [W3C PROV-N](bblocks://ogc.ogc-utils.prov.w3c-prov-n) |
| PROV-XML | [W3C PROV-XML](bblocks://ogc.ogc-utils.prov.w3c-prov-xml) |

The expanded JSON-LD retains named bundles and PROV-Links terms. It is an RDF serialization,
rather than the compact statement layout defined by the PROV-JSONLD submission.

The captured [packed CWL](examples/prov/packed.cwl),
[job inputs](examples/prov/primary-job.json), and directory metadata are also retained.
These metadata copies are not a complete BagIt archive: the hashed data payloads and the original
BagIt checksum manifests are not included. Relative `arcp:` references retain the original
research-object identity; they are not live hirondelle download URLs.
